note: Paraphrased from Ethan's post on tailoring for a big build (181 cm, 100-105 kg, 46" chest / 39" waist). He is one of the larger dressers Derek Guy interviewed for Mr Porter.

rules.rule: Choose a rise deep enough to sit and stand without hitching; a higher back rise keeps the shirt tucked.
rules.why: A bigger man's hips and seat sit higher; skimpy hip-riding trousers slide under the stomach.
rules.check: Sit down: the waistband should not dig in or drop at the back, and the shirt should stay tucked.

rules.rule: Wear braces rather than a belt, with the waistband about 1.5 cm loose when standing.
rules.why: Trousers hung from the shoulders drape cleanly; a belt cinched under the stomach bunches the leg.
rules.check: Standing, you can slip two fingers into the waistband; seated, it does not cut in.

rules.rule: Keep room through the thigh and upper leg, then taper moderately to the hem.
rules.why: A grabbing thigh strains the back rise and creases at the inseam; an extreme taper makes a pear shape over a thin ankle.
rules.check: Seated, no horizontal pull lines across the thigh; the hem width looks in scale with your shoe.

rules.rule: Use one or two pleats on a medium-to-high waist, never on a low waist.
rules.why: Pleats open when you sit and close when you stand, breaking up the lap and slimming the front.
rules.check: Standing, pleats lie closed and flat; if they splay open, the waist is too tight.

rules.rule: Finish with a gentle front break covering the top two or three eyelets, and a deeper cuff.
rules.why: A cuff adds weight so the trouser sits on the shoe; overly long, full legs flap.
rules.check: From the side, the hem rests on the shoe with one soft fold.

rules.rule: Prefer a slightly extended, soft shoulder and a softly draped chest.
rules.why: A longer shoulder line visually balances a larger waist and creates a chest-to-waist drop; drape reads relaxed rather than strained.
rules.check: The sleeve falls cleanly from the shoulder with no divot; the chest shows soft vertical folds, not pulling.

rules.rule: Generous lapels and double-breasted fronts suit a fuller girth.
rules.why: The wide overlap and lapel are in scale with a big frame; they only overwhelm smaller men.
rules.check: Lapel width looks proportional to the chest, not like a narrow strip.

rules.rule: Consider a three-piece suit in dark cloth with a short, trim waistcoat over high-waisted trousers.
rules.why: The waistcoat smooths the midsection and covers the trouser waist; dark cloth emphasises verticals.
rules.check: No shirt shows between waistcoat and trouser waistband.

rules.rule: Avoid ankle-choking jeans, bermudas and clingy T-shirts.
rules.why: Shrunken casualwear exaggerates girth and shortens the leg line.
rules.check: Casual trousers keep a straight or gently tapered leg; tops skim rather than cling.

rules.rule: Choose shoes with some visual weight: rounder toes, thicker soles, a slightly taller heel.
rules.why: Dainty, sleek shoes look undersized under a heavy frame.
rules.check: From a distance the shoe should anchor the trouser, not disappear under it.
